answer.comparison: For programming comfort under $120, the WIRED-tested Logitech MX Master 4 is the best all-round ergonomic wireless pick, while the Logitech MX Vertical is the top vertical option for reducing wrist strain and the MX Ergo S is a good space-saving trackball alternative for small desks.[1][5][3]

candidates.name: Logitech MX Master 4
keySpecs: Wireless ergonomic, best all-round coding work
candidates.reason: Best fit if you want one comfortable, feature-rich wireless mouse for long programming sessions, including fast scrolling and customizable shortcuts for code navigation.[3][1] It’s positioned as the “best overall” programming choice and is an ergonomic comfort upgrade in WIRED’s review.[3][1]

candidates.name: Logitech MX Vertical
candidates.reason: Choose this if your main issue is wrist fatigue: it’s explicitly recommended for wrist strain via its 57-degree vertical “handshake” posture.[3][5] It’s also listed as a top vertical developer-friendly ergonomic option within the $120 budget.[2]

candidates.name: Logitech MX Ergo S
keySpecs: Pairs via BT or Logi Bolt
candidates.reason: Best if you have a crowded desk or want less arm movement: it’s a programming-focused “best trackball for a small desk” with adjustable tilt and a precision mode for fine control.[3] WIRED also highlights its robust, precise trackball feel and strong build quality.[1]
